slides.title: Welcome and Framing — a Gate, Not a Graduation

items.text: Last week we commissioned the families. Tonight we commission the Companions — and this is not a graduation. Nobody is leaving; tonight opens a door further in.
The seniors become FC1 — Formation Companion, Level One: a serving place in this body. Not finishing something — beginning something.
The final rep — the container opened and closed from memory, no script
The three rules that never bend, read aloud to the whole room
The covering named — the adult each new FC1 calls when they are over their head
The commissioning — blessing spoken over each one, and the first Leader Lab on the calendar before anyone leaves

slides.title: The Final Rep — the Container Opened

items.text: Container fluency is FC1’s spine competency — Safe, Present, Clear, Intentional, from memory, without a script. Tonight is the witness of it, not the exam.
One senior opens the container whole — welcome, phones, the standing circle, one-word check-in, put out / bring in, the spoken commitment, opening prayer
“I am here. I am paying attention. I am willing to be moved.”
Every other senior speaks one condition from memory — in their own words, with one short true story of holding it while leading this year
One senior is held in reserve — tonight’s close is theirs
The gate is fluency across the arc, not perfection tonight. A stumble is not a fail.
Count the generations: Paul. Timothy. Faithful ones. Others also. Four generations in a single sentence — and the handing happens “in the presence of many witnesses.” In a room like this one.
Tonight the third generation stands up in front of the second — and the fourth is already sitting in the room
1 Timothy 4:12 — “Let no one despise you for your youth, but set the believers an example in speech, in conduct, in love, in faith, in purity.”
Tonight this room does the opposite of despising. Then prayer over the seniors.

panel.label: 2 TIMOTHY 2:2
lines: “and what you have heard from me in the presence of many witnesses entrust to faithful men, who will be able to teach others also.”

items.text: The bright line made public — the whole room hears the boundaries its young leaders keep. These rules protect you and your kids as much as they protect the leaders.
A Companion-in-Formation never counts as one of the two adults. “Co-lead” means an adult Companion in the room — not nearby, in the room.
A Companion-in-Formation never takes a disclosure. If something heavy surfaces, their only job is to hand it to the adult immediately. They are not a junior counselor.
Lead only a block you have first received. See it, then lead it.
These rules never bend — not for talent, not for maturity, not for a short-handed night. Handing the heavy thing to your adult is the strong, faithful move — never a failure.
An FC1 never leads uncovered — an adult with a name and a phone number, who has said yes
A covering that is public is a covering that holds
Each senior stands and says it plainly: “When I am over my head, I call _____.”
The sign-off confirmed publicly — the parent: “I confirm it.” The Lead Companion: “And I confirm it.”
The covering name goes onto the Commissioning Card, there in the circle — ink, not intention
Each senior stands in the center; their family stands behind them
Two Companions speak their prepared blessings — drawn from specific moments of leading: what we saw, what we bless, what we see coming
The parent may add one sentence. One. It will be the one the teen remembers.
The cohort speaks the Aaronic blessing over the new FC1 — the whole room, slowly, hands extended
“[Name], the team commissions you as Formation Companion, Level One. Serve the body. Keep the rules. Call your covering. Watch the signs.”

Then the charge, once, over all of them — keep your own walk first; keep the three rules when no one is checking; call your covering early, not late; watch the three signs. “FC1 is a real and honorable place to stand… Set the example. Begin.”
Before anyone reaches for a coat — one piece of business, on purpose, in front of everyone
The first Leader Lab of the spring serving cycle: [day], [date], [time], [place]. Write it down now.
The Lab 1 assignment is already set: bring one vital-signs observation from this room, tonight
“Anyone can hold a beautiful ceremony. The proof that tonight was a gate and not a ceremony is a date on a calendar.” The exit is an entrance.

slides.title: The Final Rep — the Container Closed

items.text: The reserved senior closes the container from memory — the standing circle, the one-word landing, the one thing, the one practice, the blessing round, the closing prayer and sending
The rite that opened in a senior’s voice ends in a senior’s voice — the last words of Getting Started are spoken by the generation it raised
If the senior sends the room, the room is sent — nothing is added after
After: the signing — everyone signs each new FC1’s keepsake, the way you sign a Bible flyleaf. Then dessert. Stay.
